## Classes

### `AuditLogEntity`

AuditLogEntity — generic audit trail entity.

Maps to any audit table (customers_audit, organizations_audit, user_profiles_audit, etc.)
via the `tableName` override option on finders/writers.

All audit tables share the same column structure:
  id          bigint identity PK
  entity_id   bigint (the audited entity's ID)
  entity_uuid uuid    (the audited entity's UUID)
  action      text    (INSERT, UPDATE, SOFT_DELETE, HARD_DELETE, RESTORE)
  changed_at  timestamptz
  changed_by  text    (actor UUID or "system")
  version     integer
  delta       jsonb   (field-level old/new diff)

This entity has NO

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| id | `bigint` |  |
| entity_id | `bigint` |  |
| entity_uuid | `string` |  |
| action | `string` |  |
| changed_at | `Date` |  |
| changed_by | `string` |  |
| version | `number` |  |
| delta | `Record<string, { old: unknown; new: unknown }>` |  |

### `BulkTimeoutError`

Thrown when a bulk write exceeds its wall-clock budget
(`DalConfig.bulkTimeoutMs` or `BulkOptions.timeoutMs`). The surrounding
transaction is rolled back — no partial writes survive.

Code: `ERR06`. TS-originated (the JS deadline fires between
statements; a slow single statement is bounded by `SET LOCAL
statement_timeout` → PG `57014` query_canceled). HTTP 408.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| code | `"ERR06"` |  |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| message | `string` |  |

### `ConfigEntityBase`

ConfigEntityBase — standard dictionary-style config table entity.

Every Primebrick config table (BE `auth_configurations`, microservice `config`)
extends this base class to get the standard column set without copy-paste.

Columns:
  key            varchar(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE — stable snake_case setting key
  value          text nullable                 — raw TEXT; null = "not set"
  type           varchar(50)  NOT NULL         — ConfigType (drives SDK coercion + FE widget)
  type_config    text nullable                 — JSONB-text extra per-type config (badge values, list API URL, etc.)
  label_key      varchar(100) nullable         — i18n key for the setting title
  description_key varchar(100) nullable        — i18n key for the explanatory text
  reserved       boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false — if true: editable but not deletable
  group_key      varchar(100) nullable         — UI grouping key (null/empty = ungrouped, top of list)

Plus standard audit columns (created_at/by, updated_at/by, version, deleted_at/by).

The consumer creates a concrete subclass:
  @Entity("config", "public")
  export class ConfigEntryEntity extends ConfigEntityBase &#123;&#125;

This class is DB-agnostic — it does NOT import from @primebrick/sdk.
The SDK's IConfigEntity interface mirrors the field names for port-level use.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| id | `bigint` |  |
| uuid | `string` |  |
| key | `string` | Unique config key (e.g. "oidc_issuer_url", "enable_mfa"). Never renamed after release. |
| value | `string \| null` | Raw TEXT value. null means "the row exists but the value is not set". |
| type | `string` | Config value type — drives SDK coercion and FE widget selection. |
| type_config | `string \| null` | JSONB-text extra per-type configuration (e.g. badge inline values, list API URL). |
| label_key | `string` | i18n key for the setting title. |
| description_key | `string` | i18n key for the explanatory description. |
| reserved | `boolean` | If true, the row is system-critical: editable but not deletable. |
| group_key | `string \| null` | Optional grouping key for UI display. null/empty = ungrouped (top of list). |
| created_at | `Date` |  |

#### `Dal.getPool(): Pool`

The underlying pg.Pool. Exposed for snapshot/migration tooling that needs raw access.

#### `Dal.close(timeoutMs): Promise<void>`

Graceful shutdown — drains the pool with a timeout deadline.

- Re-entrant: concurrent calls return immediately (the first call wins).
- Timeout: if pool.end() doesn't complete within timeoutMs, the promise
  resolves anyway (the pool is left to be reaped by the OS/TCP stack).
- Error containment: if pool.end() throws, the error is logged and swallowed.
- Does NOT install process.on() handlers — that is a consumer-side concern.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| timeoutMs | `number` | Maximum time to wait for pool.end() to complete. Default: 10000. |

#### `Dal.entityService(cfg): EntityService<TEntity>`

The public path to the generic entity-service worker. The gateway
injects its own (schema-domain-guarded, pool-scoped) Repository — the
consumer never sees it. `cfg.repo` exists only as a decorator seam
(e.g. BE `withCache`): leave it unset for the standard wiring.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| cfg | `EntityServiceConfig<TEntity>` |  |

#### `Dal.tableAuditPort(): AuditPort`

The standard `{table}_audit` writer port, bound to the gateway
Repository. Use for adapters that need an AuditPort without exposing
the Repository itself.

#### `Dal.serverVersion(): Promise<{ server_version: string; version: string }>`

Server version + connectivity probe in one call. A successful response
already proves the connection is alive — there is deliberately no
separate `ping()` (a dedicated `SELECT 1` would be a redundant round-trip).
Throws on connectivity/timeout failure.

#### `Dal.transaction(fn, options): Promise<TResult>`

Atomic multi-statement work — `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` around a
tx-scoped Repository. Use for cascades, multi-write units, and any
sequence that must commit or fail as one. Post-commit side effects
(cache invalidation, events) belong AFTER this resolves, never inside.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| fn | `(txRepo: Repository) => Promise<TResult>` |  |
| options | `TimeoutOverrideOptions` |  |

#### `Dal.beginTransaction(options): DeferredTransaction`

Deferred fluent transaction — buffer repository ops (`tx.add`, `tx.update`,
`tx.find`, …) without executing, then `tx.commit()` compiles and runs them
as ONE data-modifying CTE statement. Atomicity is PostgreSQL's
single-statement guarantee — no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and no rollback
path exist in this mode. Inter-op values flow via `Deferred.ref()`;
conditional TS logic on mid-flow results stays in `transaction(fn)`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| options | `TimeoutOverrideOptions` |  |

#### `Dal.truncate(entity, options): Promise<void>`

Physical table reset — delegates to `Repository.truncate` (entity-resolved,
schema-domain guarded). For auditable tables prefer soft-delete; TRUNCATE
is for caches, KB stores, and test teardown.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| entity | `EntityClass` |  |
| options | `{ restartIdentity: boolean; cascade: boolean }` |  |

#### `Dal.partitionMaintenance(entities, options): Promise<PartitionMaintenanceReport>`

pg_partman retention executor — metadata-driven, identical for every
service. Purges `@PartitionChildOf` children of expired parents (before
the partition drop), removes expired strays from the default partition,
then runs `partman.run_maintenance_proc()`. Called by the service's
`jobs.due.system.<svc>.partition-maintenance` consumer.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| entities | `typeOperator` | the service's entity registry (only `@PartitionField`
  entities participate; everything else is ignored) |
| options | `TimeoutOverrideOptions` |  |

### `Decimal`

### `Deferred`

Handle for a buffered operation's future result. NOT a Promise — awaiting
it pre-commit would deadlock (commit is never reached), so it deliberately
exposes no `then`. Read `.value` only after `await tx.commit()`.

#### `Deferred.ref(field): DeferredFieldRef<T[K]>`

Reference a RETURNING/SELECT column of this op for use in a LATER op.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| field | `K` |  |

### `DeferredFieldRef`

Opaque marker produced by `Deferred.ref("field")` — embeddable in a later
op's payload/match values. At compile time the `$n` it would occupy is
rewritten to `(SELECT "field" FROM "__rN")` over the source op's RETURNING
branch. Never a bound parameter — survives `jsValueToPgParam` untouched.

#### `DeferredTransaction.commit(): Promise<void>`

Compile every buffered op into ONE statement and execute it. Atomicity
is the statement's own: a failure anywhere (constraint, pg_raise guard,
abort branch, timeout) rolls back every branch — no rollback code exists
because none is needed. Resolves when all `Deferred` handles are
materialized; rejects with the first failure.

#### `DeferredTransaction.discard()`

Abandon the buffer without executing anything. Nothing has run yet by
design — this simply invalidates the transaction and its Deferred handles.

### `DeletedRecordConflictError`

Unique-constraint conflict on a soft-deleted row — the row exists with
`deleted_at` set and must be restored, never duplicated.

PG-originated via `pg_raise('ERR05', ...)`; the existing row's `uuid`
travels in the error `detail` so consumers can offer a direct restore.
This class is provided for ergonomic `instanceof` checks.

Code: `ERR05`. HTTP 409.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| code | `"ERR05"` |  |

| Parameter | Type | Description |

### `DuplicateRecordError`

Unique-constraint conflict on a live row.

Normally PG-originated: the `add()` conflict-reporting CTE calls
`pg_raise('ERR04', ...)`, and node-postgres propagates it as a
`DatabaseError` with `err.code === 'ERR04'` and a jsonb `err.detail`
(`{ entity, table, uuid, constraint }`). The DAL throws this class only
when the conflict cannot be attributed to any identifiable row (unique
group whose attempted values are all DB-generated, e.g. a payload-less
`uuid`). Provided in both cases for ergonomic `instanceof` checks.

Code: `ERR04`. HTTP 409.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| code | `"ERR04"` |  |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|

### `OptimisticLockError`

TS wrapper for the PG-originated `ERR01` optimistic concurrency violation.

The DAL does NOT throw this class in the happy/conflict path — PostgreSQL
raises `RAISE EXCEPTION ... USING ERRCODE = 'ERR01'` and node-postgres
propagates it as a `DatabaseError` with `err.code === 'ERR01'`. This class
is provided only for ergonomic `instanceof` checks if a consumer wants to
normalize PG errors into TS errors at a boundary.

Code: `ERR01`. PG-originated. HTTP 409.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| code | `"ERR01"` |  |

### `RecordVanishedError`

Thrown when an auditable-entity write matches zero rows AND a disambiguation
SELECT confirms the row no longer exists (was hard-deleted by another writer).

Code: `ERR03`. TS-originated. HTTP 404.

Distinct from `NotFoundError` (which is for finders): `ERR03` specifically
means "the row existed when you read it but is now gone".

#### `Repository.vectorSearch(entity, vectorField, queryVector, options): Promise<TResult & { similarity: number; distance: number }[]>`

pgvector nearest-neighbour search — the DAL-native replacement for raw
`<=>`-style similarity queries.

Emits `ORDER BY <vectorField> <op> $n::vector LIMIT <topK>` with the
query vector always bound as a parameter (required for HNSW/ivfflat
index usage — never interpolated). Entity-generic: schema, tableName
override, filters, projections and soft-delete scoping behave exactly
like `findAll`.

The result carries a `similarity` score column when `distance` is the
default `"<=>"` (cosine — `1 - distance`, higher = closer). For other
operators the projected column is `distance` (raw distance, lower =
closer).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| entity | `EntityClass` |  |
| vectorField | `FieldRef<TEntity, typeOperator & string>` |  |
| queryVector | `string \| number[]` |  |

### `TranslationEntityBase`

TranslationEntityBase — standard i18n translations table entity.

Schema = module boundary. Each module creates a concrete subclass with its
own schema. The DAL's Repository resolves the schema natively via
getQualifiedTableName(entity) — no raw SQL, no string interpolation.

BE creates entity classes for all modules it manages:
  @Entity("translations", "public")
  export class AppTranslationEntity extends TranslationEntityBase &#123;&#125;

  @Entity("translations", "system")
  export class SystemTranslationEntity extends TranslationEntityBase &#123;&#125;

  @Entity("translations", "emailsender")
  export class EmailsenderTranslationEntity extends TranslationEntityBase &#123;&#125;

The BE's central CRUD handler maps module code → entity class → Repository.
US microservices do NOT create entity classes — the BE manages their schemas.

Columns:
  key       varchar(255) NOT NULL — full dot-path (e.g. 'app.auth.login.title')
  language  varchar(10)  NOT NULL — BCP 47 tag (e.g. 'it-IT')
  value     text         NOT NULL — translated string

Composite unique: (key, language) — non-partial index: a soft-deleted row
still reserves the key; recreating it surfaces a conflict (ERR05 → restore),
never a deleted+live duplicate.

Plus standard audit columns (created_at/by, updated_at/by, version, deleted_at/by).

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| id | `bigint` |  |
| uuid | `string` |  |

| language | `string` | BCP 47 language tag (e.g. 'it-IT', 'en-GB'). |
| value | `string` | Translated string value. |
| created_at | `Date` |  |
| created_by | `string` |  |
| updated_at | `Date` |  |
| updated_by | `string` |  |
| version | `number` |  |
| deleted_at | `Date` |  |

### `Vector`

`Vector` — runtime-identifiable `number[]` for pgvector `vector(N)` columns.

A real class (not a brand) so the DAL can detect it with `instanceof` —
array subclasses ARE `number[]`-assignable but carry runtime identity.
That identity is load-bearing: `vector` params bind as the `'[v1,v2,…]'`
literal, while plain `number[]` binds as a Postgres array `'{v1,v2,…}'`.

In entities, `embedding: Vector` maps to `vector`; `@Column({ length: N })`
sets the dimension (`vector(N)`).

#### `Vector.toString(): string`

`'[1,2,3]'` — the pgvector text input/output literal.

#### `Vector.from(v): Vector`

Parse the pgvector literal `'[v1,v2,…]'` (or a plain number array).

### `DalConfig`

Configuration for the Dal gateway.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| connectionString | `string` | PostgreSQL connection string. Required. |
| schemas | `string[]` | Declared schema domain — the ONLY PostgreSQL schemas this service may
touch (from `DATABASE_SCHEMA`). `schemas[0]` is the owned/primary schema
(patch registry, config_entries live here). Entity operations resolving
outside this set throw SchemaDomainViolationError. Required. |
| sharedTables | `string[]` | Shared table names exempt from the schema-domain check — governed
cross-schema table contracts where every module schema carries the
same table and a designated manager reaches all of them. Today only
`translations` (the BE i18n gateway manages `<module>.translations`
for every registered module). The entity's schema pin still applies —
only the domain check is bypassed, for that table name only. |
| max | `number` | Maximum pool size. Default: 10.
 Formula: max ≤ (PG max_connections − reserved) / service_instances.
 The lib cannot pick this for you, but it documents it. |
| statementTimeoutMs | `number` | Per-statement timeout in ms, set via SET statement_timeout on every connection.
 Default: 30000. Set to 0 to disable.
 This is the full wall-clock (command arrival → server completion → all rows transmitted). |
| bulkTimeoutMs | `number` | Maximum wall-clock budget in ms for a single *Many operation
 (addMany/upsertMany/updateMany/deleteMany). The whole transaction must
 complete within this budget — on expiry the work is aborted and the
 transaction rolled back (no partial writes).
 Default: 1800000 (30 min). Per-call override: `BulkOptions.timeoutMs`.
 Set to 0 to disable. |
| connectionTimeoutMillis | `number` | Time to wait when acquiring a connection from the pool before erroring.
 Default: 5000. Fail fast when pool exhausted — don't let requests queue forever. |
| idleTimeoutMillis | `number` | How long an idle connection is kept before closing. Default: 30000 (pg default). |
| maxUses | `number` | Optional: recycle connections after N uses to clear per-session state.
 Default: undefined (off). |
| applicationName | `string` | Optional application_name for PG logging/observability. Default: "primebrick-dal". |
| repoDecorator | `(repo: Repository) => Repository` | Optional decorator applied to the Dal's internal root Repository at
construction — the governed seam for cross-cutting behavior such as
entity caching (`withCache`). The decorated repo backs `dal.entityService`,
`dal.tableAuditPort`, and every entity proxy on this instance, so the
decoration applies uniformly without consumers building their own
repositories. Tx-scoped repositories handed to `dal.transaction(fn)`
callbacks are NOT decorated — writes inside an open transaction must
not trigger cache writes/invalidation before commit. |

### `EntityClass`

Entity metadata via legacy TypeScript decorators (WeakMap "reflection").

**Convention:** every "data" property on the class `prototype` is a SQL column
with a name equal to the property name (snake_case). `@Column()` is only needed
for: `sqlName` / `pgType` / `nullable`, or a short alias for the column name.

- `@Entity()` — table name; optional argument if different from class name.
- `@Key()` — primary key (one column only).
- `@Unique()` — unique index (DDL patch).
- `@IsNotColumn()` — excludes the property from persistence meta & DAL queries.
- `@AuditableField(type)` — marks a field as audit (created_at, created_by, etc.).
- `@DeletableField(type)` — marks a field as soft-delete (deleted_at, deleted_by).
- `@CloneField()` — marks a field as clone tracking (cloned_from).
- `@AuditTrail()` — marks the entity as having an audit trail table.

**Type:** `(args: any[]) => object`

### `ExprOperand`

A parameterized SQL operand for `Filter.expr` — `?` markers inside `sql`
are replaced by `$n` bound parameters in order of appearance.

`sql` is a trusted literal (never interpolated user input); `params`
carries the only dynamic data. Example:
  `{ sql: "to_tsvector(?, d.content)", params: ["simple"] }`

### `PgScalarType`

`PgColumnType` — the canonical PostgreSQL column type vocabulary for
`@Column({ pgType })` and the entity type contract.

A closed union, not a free `string`: aliases like
`"timestamp with time zone"` (write `timestamptz`) or `"character varying"`
(write `varchar`) are compile errors, so the diff/snapshot pipeline never
sees spelling variants.

Type modifiers are NEVER written inside `pgType`: `varchar(N)` comes from
`length`, `numeric(p,s)` from `precision`/`scale`, `vector(N)` from
`length` on a `Vector` prop. `pgType` carries the BASE name only
(`vector(N)` literal is allowed for readability but `length` wins).

**Type:** `"text" \| "varchar" \| "char" \| "citext" \| "uuid" \| "smallint" \| "int2" \| "integer" \| "int" \| "int4" \| "bigint" \| "int8" \| "real" \| "float4" \| "double precision" \| "float8" \| "numeric" \| "decimal" \| "boolean" \| "bool" \| "date" \| "time" \| "timetz" \| "timestamp" \| "timestamptz" \| "interval" \| "inet" \| "cidr" \| "macaddr" \| "macaddr8" \| "json" \| "jsonb" \| "bytea" \| "xml" \| "tsvector"`

## Constants

### `DalErrorCodes`

Stable error codes for DAL optimistic concurrency control.

These codes are used as PostgreSQL SQLSTATE values (via `RAISE EXCEPTION
USING ERRCODE = 'ERR01'`) and as TS `DalError.code` values. Consumers (BE,
US, FE) branch on the string literal (e.g. `err.code === 'ERR01'`) so that
PG-originated errors and TS-originated errors share the same code.

Convention: `ERR` + 2 digits. The `ER` class is outside the SQL-standard
SQLSTATE classes (`00`–`99`), so PostgreSQL accepts it as a custom code.

**Type:** `{ ERR01: "ERR01"; ERR02: "ERR02"; ERR03: "ERR03"; ERR04: "ERR04"; ERR05: "ERR05"; ERR06: "ERR06"; ERR07: "ERR07"; ERR08: "ERR08"; ERR09: "ERR09"; ERR10: "ERR10" }`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| ERR01 | "ERR01" |
| ERR02 | "ERR02" |
| ERR03 | "ERR03" |
| ERR04 | "ERR04" |
| ERR05 | "ERR05" |
| ERR06 | "ERR06" |
| ERR07 | "ERR07" |
| ERR08 | "ERR08" |
| ERR09 | "ERR09" |
| ERR10 | "ERR10" |

Marks a class as BEING an audit trail entity (e.g., AuditLogEntity).

### `buildAuditableJoins(entity, userEntity): JoinExpr[]`

Standard join configuration for auditable entities.
Automatically adds LEFT JOINs to the user entity table for created_by, updated_by, deleted_by fields.

Uses regex guardrail pattern to only join when the field contains a valid UUID.
This prevents errors when the field contains non-UUID values like "system".

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| entity | `EntityClass` | The entity class implementing IAuditableEntity |
| userEntity | `EntityClass` | The user entity class (e.g. UserProfileEntity) that has a `uuid` and `display_name` column |

### `buildAuditableJoinsSelective(entity, userEntity, options): JoinExpr[]`

Enhanced version that allows selective joins (e.g., only creator and updater).
Useful when you only need specific audit fields to reduce query overhead.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| entity | `EntityClass` | The entity class implementing IAuditableEntity |
| userEntity | `EntityClass` | The user entity class (e.g. UserProfileEntity) |
| options | `{ includeCreator: boolean; includeUpdater: boolean; includeDeleter: boolean }` | Configuration for which joins to include |

### `buildAuditTrailJoins(auditEntity, userEntity): { joins: JoinExpr[]; projections: FieldProjector[] }`

Build LEFT JOIN + projections for audit trail entities (AuditLogEntity).

Audit trail entities have a single `changed_by` column (not created_by/updated_by/deleted_by).
This function joins the user entity to resolve `changed_by` into `display_name` and `idp_code`.

Uses `castRightTo: "uuid"` + `castLeftTo: "uuid"` to trigger the regex guardrail
(`changed_by ~ '^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}$'`) automatically in renderJoins().
This prevents errors when `changed_by` contains non-UUID values like "system".

Distinct from buildAuditableJoins() which uses castRightTo: "text" (no guardrail, text = text).
buildAuditTrailJoins() uses castRightTo: "uuid" + castLeftTo: "uuid" (guardrail + uuid = uuid).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| auditEntity | `EntityClass` | The audit trail entity class (e.g., AuditLogEntity) |
| userEntity | `EntityClass` | The user entity class (e.g., UserProfileEntity) with uuid, display_name, idp_code columns |

### `ForeignKey(target, opts): PropertyDecorator`

Declares a FOREIGN KEY constraint referencing another entity's column.
`target` is a lazy thunk (`() => CustomerEntity`) so circular entity
references resolve at meta-read time, not class-eval time.
Minimal form `@ForeignKey(() => CustomerEntity)` references the target's
`@Key()` column with `ON DELETE RESTRICT` / `ON UPDATE NO ACTION` —
the zero-option path is the safest behavior.
Note: a partitioned parent (`@PartitionField`) cannot be a plain FK target
unless the referenced unique constraint includes the partition key —
meta validation throws and points to `@PartitionChildOf` for that shape.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| target | `() => EntityClass` |  |
| opts | `ForeignKeyOptions` |  |

### `getDal(config): Dal`

Returns the process-wide singleton Dal instance. Creates it on first call.

- First call: requires `config`, creates the singleton.
- Subsequent calls with NO config: returns the existing instance.
- Subsequent calls with the SAME connectionString: returns the existing instance.
- Subsequent calls with a DIFFERENT connectionString: throws (prevents accidental
  double-init with wrong params).

For multi-DB: construct `new Dal(config)` directly (bypasses the singleton).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| config | `DalConfig` |  |

### `Index(): PropertyDecorator`

Declares a secondary (non-unique) index. Bare `@Index()` → single-column
btree auto-named `<table>_<col>_idx`. Same `name` on multiple columns →
composite index ordered by `order`. Supports every PG access method:
`@Index({ using: 'hnsw', opclass: 'vector_cosine_ops' })`,
`@Index({ where: 'deleted_at IS NULL' })` for partial indexes.
Unique indexes stay on `@Unique()`.

### `normalizePatchEol(body): string`

Patch integrity hashes are EOL-insensitive: a Windows checkout may
materialize CRLF while the committed blob and the signed MANIFEST are LF.
Normalize before hashing so manifest verification and the patch registry
are platform-stable.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| body | `string` |  |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| raw | `string` |  |

### `parsePatchSegments(raw): PatchSegment[]`

Split a patch file into execution segments. Default content is transactional
(`tx`); statements inside `-- pb:begin-no-transaction` … `-- pb:end-no-transaction`
run per-statement in autocommit (for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY & friends).
Whole-file `-- pb:no-transaction` is equivalent to wrapping everything.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| raw | `string` |  |

### `PartitionChildOf(opts): ClassDecorator`

Declares this entity a logical child of a `@PartitionField`-partitioned
parent: it joins the parent's atomic delete and retention purge unit.
Needed because a partitioned parent cannot host a plain FOREIGN KEY
(unique constraints must contain the partition key) — the relationship
is application-level, enforced by the repository cascade and the
partition-maintenance purge. Entities that merely REFERENCE a parent
(telemetry, logs) simply don't declare this.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| opts | `PartitionChildOfOptions` |  |

### `PartitionField(opts): PropertyDecorator`

Marks a column as the RANGE partition key of the table (pg_partman,
monthly/daily/…). Exactly ONE per entity. The column must be NOT NULL and
date/timestamptz-typed; every unique group and the primary key emitted in
DDL must include it (PostgreSQL requirement) — `getEntityPersistenceMeta`
validates this and throws otherwise, so a partitioned entity can never
produce an invalid table definition.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| opts | `PartitionFieldOptions` |  |

### `splitSqlStatements(sql): string[]`

Top-level SQL statement splitter for `-- pb:no-transaction` segments.

Needed because node-pg's simple query protocol executes a multi-statement
string in a single implicit transaction — to get per-statement autocommit
(required for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY etc.) statements must be sent
separately. Handles: single/double-quoted strings, dollar-quoted bodies
($$…$$, $tag$…$tag$), line comments, block comments.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| sql | `string` |  |
